title: Repel with better
hookLine: repel evil with what is better, and your enemy may become a close friend (41:34)

lines: A MAN YANKS THE PROPHET'S CLOAK.
cards: A man from the desert catches up with the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, grabs his cloak, and yanks it so hard the thick border leaves a mark where his neck meets his shoulder.
Then he says: give me some of the wealth of Allah that you have. Anas, walking beside him, says the Prophet turned to the man, and smiled. Then he ordered that the man be given something.
Teachers often set that scene, from Sahih al-Bukhari, beside a verse in Surah Fussilat.

teach.h: GOOD AND EVIL ARE NOT ALIKE.

teach.b: Pickthall: "The good deed and the evil deed are not alike. Repel the evil deed with one which is better, then lo! he, between whom and thee there was enmity (will become) as though he was a bosom friend."
First: good and evil aren't the same. Obvious, but it matters: the verse isn't saying harm doesn't count.
Then the instruction: idfa', push back. It's an active verb. You do respond.
With what? Bi'llati hiya ahsan, with what is better. Not just good: better than what was done to you, and better than what you were about to do back.
Then the promise, and the word for friend is striking: waliyyun hamim. Hamim is also the word for something hot. A warm friend, someone whose friendship has heat in it.
The enemy doesn't just stop being an enemy; he might become that. Notice the as though in Pickthall's wording: a likeness, not a guarantee. Verse thirty-five is honest about how hard this is.

teach.h: ONLY THE PATIENT ARE GIVEN IT.
teach.b: Only the patient are given it, and only someone with a great share of good.

Ibn 'Abbas is reported to have explained it this way: Allah commands patience at anger, gentleness at ignorance, and forgiveness at harm, and when people do that, their enemy submits to them like a close friend.
Fussilat means explained in detail. This is one of the details: what to do when someone yanks the cloak.

how: Muslim teachers often cite 41:34 together with stories of the Prophet's patience toward people who wronged him, as guidance for answering insults and family quarrels with kindness.

o: strike back, matching harm with equal harm
step away, leaving a quarrel without a word
push back, answering harm with something better

games.q: repel with better — tap the pairs.
p: the man who pulled the cloak

s: the verse says good and evil are the same in the end
its first line: the good deed and the evil deed are not alike.
hamim is also a word for something hot
a waliyyun hamim is a warm friend, a friendship with heat in it.
the verse says this is easy for anyone
verse thirty-five: only the patient are given it.

games.q: a man yanks the Prophet's cloak so hard it leaves a mark, and demands money. what does the Prophet do?
o: turns, smiles, and has him given something.
games.why: Anas reports in Bukhari that the Prophet turned, smiled, and ordered that the man be given something.

practice: Bring to mind a small recent hurt, a sharp message, a slight, a door shut in your face, and feel the reply you wanted to give.
Now look for the better one, not giving in, not pretending it didn't happen: a kind word, a small gift, a calm answer, a smile. Picture yourself giving it, and notice what happens in your chest.

wordCard.voice: Idfa', push back, Fussilat's instruction to repel harm with what is better, which can turn an enemy into a warm friend. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: repel with what is better (41:34).

carryVoice: Your line: a warm friend. Better than what was done, and better than what you'd do back. That's five hundred sixty-four.
